harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1/node2/node3 (node1 initially primary, node2/node3 standbys via pg_basebackup + replication slots). Exercised a full failover: stopped node1's postgres to simulate primary loss, promoted node2 (verified zero committed-data loss), repointed node3 to follow node2, and rebuilt node1 as a fresh standby of node2 (pg_rewind was unavailable due to missing checksums/wal_log_hints, so used pg_basebackup instead). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node1, node3, then node2 (primary) one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirming changed boot_id and full replication/data recovery after each before proceeding to the next. Final state: node2 = writable primary, node1 & node3 = streaming standbys, all caught up to the latest LSN and identical row counts/data.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 16 server/contrib via AppStream module on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all nodes
Initialized primary DB on node1; configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf for replication+client access
Generated replication password via openssl on node1 and created 'replicator' ROLE WITH REPLICATION LOGIN (password threaded via secret_env, never in command text)
Created appdb database and seed table 't' with test rows on node1
Created physical replication slots and ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 to node2 and node3, starting both as standbys
Verified streaming replication (pg_stat_replication, matching LSNs) and cross-node SELECT consistency
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgresql on node1 after confirming standbys fully caught up to latest committed LSN
Promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote; verified pg_is_in_recovery=false and all pre-failover rows intact plus new writes accepted
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo/primary_slot_name to node2 and restarted it as node2's standby; verified data consistency

Rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via fresh pg_basebackup (pg_rewind attempt failed due to missing data checksums/wal_log_hints) and started it; verified it caught up with all data including post-failover writes
Reverted temporary SUPERUSER grant on replicator role after abandoning pg_rewind path
Captured boot_id + service/data health baseline on all 3 nodes

Sequentially rebooted node1, then node3, then node2 (primary) via systemctl reboot, polling each until exec access returned, confirming boot_id changed each time and that postgresql/replication/data recovered before moving to the next node
Performed a final end-to-end write on node2 and confirmed replication to node1 and node3

evidence.requirement: Primary/standby streaming replication established (node1 primary, node2+node3 standbys)
evidence.summary: PostgreSQL started on node1 as primary; base backups taken by node2/node3 which came up pg_is_in_recovery=t; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both nodes 'streaming'

evidence.requirement: Data replicates correctly to both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 (primary) is immediately visible identically on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Failover: standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Committed row confirmed replicated (matching LSN) before node1 was stopped; node2 promoted (pg_is_in_recovery flips to f) and all 5 pre-failover rows plus a new post-failover write are present

evidence.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) re-pointed to new primary without data loss
evidence.summary: node3 reconfigured with primary_conninfo->node2 and restarted; pg_is_in_recovery=t and full row set including post-failover write confirmed present

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of new primary without data loss
evidence.summary: node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and restarted as standby; pg_is_in_recovery=t and all 6 rows including post-failover write present

evidence.requirement: Full 3-node cluster healthy post-failover (node2 primary, node1+node3 standbys, both caught up)
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node2 shows both node1 and node3 streaming and caught up to the same replay_lsn after a new write; temporary superuser grant on replicator reverted

evidence.requirement: Restart protocol - node1 (standby): healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4a743885...; reboot acknowledged, node briefly unreachable, then returned with boot_id b02b89fb... (changed) and uptime 0 min; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, data intact, and node2 shows node1 streaming again

evidence.requirement: Restart protocol - node3 (standby): healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 18d6ac04...; reboot acknowledged, connection reset mid-boot, returned with boot_id e5f6b449... (changed) and uptime 0 min; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, data intact, node2 shows node3 streaming again

evidence.requirement: Restart protocol - node2 (primary): healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state as primary with quorum/replication restored
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 54bd1c3e...; reboot acknowledged, timed out mid-boot, returned with boot_id 4369b7b1... (changed) and uptime 0 min; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=f (still primary), both node1 and node3 reconnected as streaming standbys, and a final write replicates correctly to both, confirmed identical on all three nodes
